preconditions.description: The number of users n is between 2 and 250,000 inclusive.
The number of edges in T1 is exactly n-1.
The number of edges in T2 is exactly n-1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in T1_edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge in T1 connects two users numbered between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for c, d in T2_edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge in T2 connects two users numbered between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.description: The number of protected edges m is between 0 and n-1 inclusive.
The number of protected edges in the output is exactly m.

postconditions.expression: all((a, b) in T1_edges and (c, d) in T2_edges for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)
postconditions.description: Each protected edge (a, b, c, d) consists of an edge (a, b) from T1 and an edge (c, d) from T2.

postconditions.expression: len(set((a, b) for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)) == m
postconditions.description: Each edge in T1 is protected at most once.

postconditions.expression: len(set((c, d) for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)) == m
postconditions.description: Each edge in T2 is used as a replacement at most once.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected(T1_edges - {(a, b)} | {(c, d)}) for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)
postconditions.description: After replacing each edge (a, b) in T1 with (c, d) in T2, the network remains connected.
